attachments.insertion_landmark: medial border of scapula, at the root of the spine

actions: retracts and downwardly rotates the scapula

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: Smaller and more superior than rhomboid major, sometimes fused with it as a single continuous sheet -- a documented anatomical variant.
functional_compartments.source: Holzbaur KR, Murray WM, Delp SL (2005) Ann Biomed Eng 33(6):829-840 -- upper-extremity muscle architecture model (fascicle length, pennation, PCSA)

motor_endplate_zones.method: modified Sihler staining, whole-mount nerve arborization mapping
motor_endplate_zones.notes: The medial (origin-side) third, one of two arborization-dense bands. The dorsal scapular nerve enters in the middle third (33-67%), between this zone and the lateral one -- avoid that band, since a documented case of dorsal scapular neuropathy followed an injection placed there.
motor_endplate_zones.source: Yi KH, Lee HJ, Choi YJ, Hu KS, Kim HJ, 'Intramuscular Neural Distribution of Rhomboid Muscles: Evaluation for Botulinum Toxin Injection Using Modified Sihler's Method', Toxins 12(5):289 (2020), doi:10.3390/toxins12050289 -- 30 rhomboid major + 30 minor muscles, 10 of each Sihler-stained, Korean cadavers. Retrieved via PubMed (PMC7291336).

motor_endplate_zones.method: modified Sihler staining, whole-mount nerve arborization mapping
motor_endplate_zones.notes: The lateral (insertion-side) third, the second arborization-dense band, mirroring the medial one across the avoided middle third.
motor_endplate_zones.source: Yi KH, Lee HJ, Choi YJ, Hu KS, Kim HJ, 'Intramuscular Neural Distribution of Rhomboid Muscles: Evaluation for Botulinum Toxin Injection Using Modified Sihler's Method', Toxins 12(5):289 (2020), doi:10.3390/toxins12050289 -- 30 rhomboid major + 30 minor muscles, 10 of each Sihler-stained, Korean cadavers. Retrieved via PubMed (PMC7291336).

trigger_points.location_description: Trigger points along the medial scapular border, palpated with the scapula protracted (hand across chest)
trigger_points.referred_pain_pattern: Superficial aching pain along the medial border of the scapula and the interscapular zone -- present at rest, unchanged by ordinary movement, often with snapping/crunching on scapular motion. Does not project to the arm.
trigger_points.activation_perpetuating_factors: Ache with prolonged sitting/rounded posture rather than true motion loss; fatigue holding retraction.
trigger_points.notes: This atlas's source document covers rhomboid major and minor together as a single 'Rhomboid major & minor' section without differentiating trigger points between the two muscles.
trigger_points.source: Simons, Travell & Simons Trigger Point Manual -- as cited in this atlas's uploaded shoulder muscle reference document (Donnelly JM, Fernandez-de-las-Penas C, Finnegan M, Freeman JL (eds), Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction: The Trigger Point Manual, 3rd ed., Wolters Kluwer, 2019)

clinical.function_biomechanics: Retract (adduct) the scapula and rotate it downward (with levator and pectoralis minor); fix the medial border against the thorax during arm use, eccentrically controlling protraction (punching, pushing, follow-through). Weakness/palsy → lateral drift of the scapula with mild medial-border lifting; tightness with pectoral shortening → the round-shouldered pattern that keeps them chronically overstretched and achy.
clinical.adjacent_structures: Adjacent bursae: None constant of their own; the superomedial scapulothoracic (scapulotrapezial) bursal plane lies at their upper insertion zone. Adjacent structures — mutual influence: Dorsal scapular nerve (through scalenus medius) — entrapment produces the same interscapular ache; serratus anterior partner-sling; thoracic facet/rib joints and serratus posterior superior beneath; scapulothoracic crepitus arises in this interval.

trigger_points.location: TrPs along the medial scapular border in both muscles, palpated with the scapula protracted (hand across chest).
trigger_points.referred_pain: Superficial aching pain along the medial border of the scapula and the interscapular zone — present at rest, unchanged by ordinary movement, often with snapping/crunching on scapular motion. Does not project to the arm.
trigger_points.source: Donnelly JM, Fernández-de-las-Peñas C, Finnegan M, Freeman JL (eds). Travell, Simons & Simons’ Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction: The Trigger Point Manual. 3rd ed. Wolters Kluwer; 2019. Muscle chapters as named in each section.

pain_referred_into_this_muscle_from: The interscapular area is a busy convergence zone: scaleni, levator scapulae, infraspinatus, latissimus TrP1, serratus posterior superior, middle trapezius, serratus anterior (inferior-angle spot)
C6–C7 facet and cervical discogenic pain classically refer between the scapulae (Cloward points)
visceral mimics (biliary → right interscapular; aortic/oesophageal → central).
clinical.movement_restrictions_aggravators: Ache with prolonged sitting/rounded posture rather than true motion loss; fatigue holding retraction.
clinical.notes: Interscapular pain is cervical until proven otherwise — screen C6–C7 before needling rhomboids; then fix the pec-minor/major shortness that overstretches them.
clinical.caveat: Trigger-point locations and referral maps derive from the Travell–Simons clinical-observational tradition, now standardised by Delphi consensus criteria [32] and supported by prevalence and hyperalgesia studies in shoulder pain [30,31]; they are expert-level evidence, not trial-level, and inter-examiner reliability of TrP palpation is moderate. Facet, ACJ and subacromial referral patterns, by contrast, come from experimental provocation in volunteers/patients [33,34,37]. Textbook anatomy is cited at section level; where major texts disagree (segmental levels), the range is given and flagged. Figures and patterns older than 12 months are anatomical/physiological constants and are not considered stale.
